summary: Tarragon bechamel: a roux of 4 tablespoons butter and 3 tablespoons flour cooked 2 minutes, whisked with 2 cups of milk in a thin stream, simmered about 5 minutes with salt and 1 tablespoon of minced tarragon until it coats a spoon; makes 2 cups in 15 minutes.
glance: 1 tablespoon fresh tarragon (or 1 generous teaspoon dried)
faq: What is bechamel?

A fundamental sauce of milk thickened with flour. It can be elaborated with herbs, enriched with cheese for mac and cheese, or used as the base of a creamy soup, providing richness without the excessive fat of a cream-based sauce.
How do I avoid lumps?

The most critical part is the very beginning: add the milk in a thin stream while whisking continuously, and break up any lumps before adding so much liquid that you have to chase them around the pan.
Can I use low-fat milk?
It works just fine with 2 percent milk, but the author can't recommend skim milk.
How much tarragon?
A tablespoon of minced fresh tarragon is sufficient to flavor 2 cups of sauce because tarragon is powerful. If you substitute other herbs, you'll generally want a larger quantity.
Can I make it ahead?
Use it immediately or refrigerate for up to a day. Whisk and reheat gently, adding a little more milk if needed.
Where is it used?
As a sauce in the Stuffed & Baked Polenta.

summary: A review of the children's book Whopper Cake by Karma Wilson and Will Hillenbrand, with the author's chocolate-cream cheese frosting for a 9x13 sheet cake: melted chocolate chips and butter whisked with room-temperature cream cheese and chilled about an hour.
glance: Whopper Cake by Karma Wilson, illustrated by Will Hillenbrand
enough for a 9 x 13-inch sheet cake
12 ounces chocolate chips, 4 tablespoons butter, 6 ounces cream cheese, 1/8 teaspoon salt
about an hour until firm enough to spread
faq: What is Whopper Cake about?

A grandpa wants to make a birthday cake for his wife but has trouble following the recipe, because it's too tempting to scale it up a hundred-fold; a delicious mess ensues. The book ends with a normal-scale recipe for Whopper Cake.
Is it a good book for kids who cook?
The author says to buy it for any kid who loves to cook with family, or any kid who loves cake. It was in nightly rotation before his daughter's birthday.
How is the Whopper Cake?
The author confirms it makes a very moist, tasty chocolate sheet cake. The book doesn't specify a frosting, so he developed a chocolate-cream cheese one.
How do I make the chocolate-cream cheese frosting?

Melt the chocolate chips and butter in a double boiler or microwave (1 minute at a time, stirring between), cool a bit so it won't curdle the cream cheese, whisk in the room-temperature cream cheese and salt until smooth, then refrigerate about an hour.
Is the frosting vegetarian?
The frosting is vegetarian and gluten-free but not vegan (the cake itself isn't addressed).

summary: Peppery red wine capellini cooked by the absorption method: angel hair toasted 12 minutes at 375°F, then cooked in one pot on top of zucchini, asparagus and tomatoes with red wine, smoked paprika, black pepper and herbs, tossing every 3 minutes for 8-12 minutes; serves 4.
glance: 1 pound capellini, broken in 3-inch lengths and toasted about 12 minutes
8-12 minutes covered, tossing every 3 minutes, in 1 1/4 cups red wine plus 1 1/4 cups water
faq: What is the absorption method for pasta?

Cooking pasta in a measured amount of liquid, which it absorbs, instead of boiling it in a gallon of salted water. It can be a big time saver: you don't wait for water to boil, and you may not have two pots to clean if the sauce is built in with the pasta.
Why toast the capellini first?

It is characteristic of how pasta is handled in Spain, Mexico (where it's called fideos) and the Middle East, and the author enjoys the additional browned flavors. You can do it while prepping and sauteeing the vegetables.
How do I know when it's done?

Cook covered over medium heat and every 3 minutes remove the lid and toss; the total will probably be 8 to 12 minutes. Taste a noodle each time toward the end, and if it isn't done and there's no moisture on the bottom, add maybe 1/3 cup more wine or water.
Why start with less liquid than usual?
Because the tomatoes and zucchini cook along with the noodles and release liquid, so you check along the way and add more as needed.
Is the dish mild?

No: the flavor is quite assertive with substantial red wine, black pepper, smoked paprika and garlic, so the author wouldn't necessarily recommend it for young children or those who prefer milder tastes.
Why reserve some tomatoes?
Reserved raw cherry tomatoes garnish the dish: the author loves to include an ingredient both cooked and fresh to experience its full range of flavors.

summary: Strawberry "shortcake" with cornbread and tarragon whipped cream: a slightly cakey vanilla cornbread baked about 25 minutes at 375°F, strawberries macerated an hour in sugar, and cream infused with bruised tarragon at least an hour before whipping; serves 4.
glance: 6 cups, macerated about an hour with 1/2 cup sugar
375°F in an 8x8 pan, about 25 minutes (makes more than you need)
infuse with tarragon at least 1 hour, overnight for stronger flavor
faq: Why use cornbread for shortcake?

Corn and strawberries go really well together, and they both speak of Americana. The author lowered the corn-to-flour ratio, skipped the brown butter and added vanilla to make the cornbread more cakey and dessert-like without being overly sweet.
How long should I macerate strawberries?

About one hour, tossing occasionally. Perfectly fresh, perfumed berries need less or no maceration; for less-good berries, a longer maceration with plenty of sugar makes them break down, be more tender and release more flavor.
How do you make tarragon whipped cream?

Bruise 4 teaspoons of tarragon leaves between your fingers, stir them into 2 cups of heavy cream and refrigerate at least an hour (overnight for stronger flavor). Strain, add 1/4 cup confectioner's sugar and whip to firm peaks.
Is tarragon whipped cream really good?
The author thought it went beautifully: the anisey intensity of the herb balances the corn and strawberries. If it violates your idea of shortcake, he accepts that, but suggests trying it.
How do I assemble it?
Cut four generous squares of cornbread, split each in half horizontally, and layer strawberries and juice between and on top, finishing with a generous portion of the whipped cream.

summary: Rye piroshki with roasted onions and Swiss cheese: a yeasted rye and all-purpose dough made from a 2-hour sponge, rolled around skillet-roasted onions with caraway and 24 ounces of grated Swiss, glazed with egg and baked at 400°F until golden; yields 8.
glance: 2-hour sponge, 10 minutes of kneading, 1 hour rise, 1 more hour resting in balls
4 large onions browned in a skillet with toasted caraway and 24 ounces grated Swiss
400°F until golden brown and oozing cheese
faq: What are piroshki?

Not to be confused with pierogi, individual yeast buns popular in Russia and all over Eastern Europe, filled with anything from potatoes and cabbage to cottage cheese and jam. They are generally made with white flour; this version uses rye.
How did this recipe come about?

The author had leftover rye pizza dough he was unhappy with as pizza and free-associated rye, Swiss, onions, caraway, then rolled it up and baked it. He first thought of calling it a Jewish deli calzone, but piroshki is a closer match.
How do I cook the onions?

Quick skillet-roasted: cook sliced onions in oil over medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until well browned but still with some crunch, then stir in caraway, cayenne, salt and pepper. Slowly caramelized onions would also be delicious but you'll need more of them.
How do I shape piroshki?

Roll each ball to about 10 by 8 inches, spoon a line of onions and cheese lengthwise about 2 inches from a long edge, leaving an inch at each end, and roll up into a torpedo shape, sealing the ends and seam. Brush with egg wash, salt and slash three times.
How do I serve them?
Hot. Cut each piroshki into 3 pieces to let them cool a little faster and make them easier to handle.

summary: A review of Ivy Manning's Crackers & Dips: More than 50 Handmade Snacks, with her recipe for Ritzy Peanut Butter (or sunflower butter) sandwich crackers: a dough with barley malt syrup chilled at least an hour, rolled 1/16 inch thick and baked at 400°F/375°F; makes 25 sandwiches.
glance: Crackers & Dips: More than 50 Handmade Snacks by Ivy Manning
Ritzy Peanut Butter (or Sunflower Butter) Sandwich Crackers: 25 sandwiches (50 crackers)
dough at least 1 hour and up to 2 days; filling 30 minutes
up to 4 days in an airtight container
faq: What is Crackers & Dips like?

A single-subject cookbook with classic, global, healthy, quick and sweet crackers plus a selection of dips and spreads, with detailed tips on mixing the doughs, which can be made ahead, and rolling them to the perfect thickness. A hand-cranked pasta maker is an awesome choice for many crackers.
Why does the author like single-subject cookbooks?
He reaches for the more specific tomes more than any other because they have both the recipes and inspiration, and the detailed techniques needed for success.
Can I make the sandwich crackers with sunflower butter?
Yes. The author made them for his wife, who has a nut allergy, substituting sunflower butter for peanut butter, and they worked perfectly. They were easy to make and came out delicious.
What is the secret to the buttery crackers?
Barley malt syrup, a sweet, thick syrup made from sprouted barley used by bakers and brewers when a light, malty flavor is desired. Dark corn syrup can substitute.
How do you bake them?

Roll the chilled dough 1/16 inch thick, cut 2 1/2-inch rounds, brush with egg, prick with a fork, sprinkle with salt and bake at 400°F for 4 minutes, rotate, then reduce to 375°F for about 8 more minutes until light golden brown and firm.
Is there a disclosure?
Ivy is a friend, an internet pal since the early days of Herbivoracious, whom the author describes as having a great palate and being a conscientious recipe author.

summary: Black rice fritters with chimichurri, a lighter Hanukkah entree: cooked and cooled black rice mixed with egg and smoked paprika, pan-fried about 2 minutes per side into 5-inch pancakes and served with a parsley, cilantro and caper chimichurri; makes 12.
glance: 3 cups cooked, cooled black rice (1 cup dry)
about 2 minutes per side in a tablespoon of oil, 1/4 cup per fritter
faq: Why make fritters for Hanukkah?

It is traditional to eat foods cooked in oil at Hanukkah, but after days of latkes and bunuelos the author wanted to lighten things up. These are pan fried for a crispy, satisfying chew without absorbing too much fat.
What black rice do I use?
The recipe was developed for Hinode, which imports a black rice from Thailand with a longer grain and lighter texture than the familiar "forbidden rice."
What is chimichurri?
An Argentine parsley sauce. This version blends olive oil, garlic, parsley, cilantro, salt, pepper and sherry vinegar, then mixes in minced red onion and capers for a bright, acidic counterpoint.
What if I don't have smoked paprika?
Omit it, or substitute a few pinches of plain paprika and cayenne, but the author strongly recommends smoked Spanish paprika for complex, smoky flavor in meatless meals.
Do I need a big food processor for the chimichurri?
A small one. If you only have a full-size machine, make a double batch, as it won't work well on this small quantity.

summary: Cherry-pumpkin seed muffins, a nut-free adaptation of a recipe from Ivy Manning's The Farm to Table Cookbook (from Pearl Bakery's Lee Posey): creamed-butter batter with pitted fresh cherries and toasted pepitas, baked at 375°F for 20-25 minutes; makes 12.
glance: 375°F for 20-25 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean
8 ounces fresh Bing or Lapin, pitted and roughly chopped
Vegetarian; not vegan or gluten-free; nut-free as written
faq: What is The Farm to Table Cookbook?
By Northwest author Ivy Manning, organized by seasons with an emphasis on ingredients you'd find at a farmer's market, with recipes from the author and a who's-who of regional chefs.
How is this nut-free?
The original is Cherry-Almond muffins. Because the author's family can't use almonds or almond extract, they substituted pumpkin seeds (pepitas) and vanilla extract.
How do I pit cherries?

The book suggests putting them in a plastic bag and smushing the pits out. The author used a simple "hole punch" style pitter, which works unless you're doing ten pounds at a time. Do it in the sink and keep the bowl of pitted cherries a foot away so no pits get mixed in.
How do I keep the muffins tender?
Mix half the flour mixture into the butter, then half the milk, then the remaining halves, and do not overbeat or the muffins will be tough.
How do I use the pumpkin seeds?
Stir 1/2 cup toasted pepitas into the batter and top the muffins with 1/4 cup raw ones.

summary: Swiss chard with garlic and yogurt for a meze spread: chard microwaved 3 minutes until wilted, shocked in ice water, squeezed dry and tossed at room temperature with garlic, olive oil, dukkah and salt, served with thick Greek yogurt and toasted sesame seeds.
glance: about 2 as a side dish (depends on the bunch), easily multiplied
microwave 3 minutes, then shock in ice water to keep the color
dukkah, or equal parts ground sesame, coriander, cumin and thyme
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan if you omit the yogurt or use soy yogurt
faq: What is meze?

The Mediterranean tradition of a meal made of several small plates. The author's family especially likes it in summer, when no one wants to heat the kitchen or eat a heavy dinner. Make a couple of items from scratch and fill out the spread with warm pita, marinated feta, olives, hummus and raw vegetables.
How do you cook the chard so it keeps color?

Wash thoroughly in at least 2 changes of water, strip the leaves from the stems, discard the toughest part of the stems and chop the rest into 1-inch lengths. Microwave leaves and stems on high for 3 minutes until wilted but not turning gray, then plunge into ice water, drain and squeeze dry in a clean dishtowel.
What is dukkah?
A spice mixture that originated in Egypt. It generally contains ground hazelnuts or other nuts, so check the ingredients of any pre-packaged version if you have a nut allergy.
What if I don't have dukkah?
Make an equal-parts mixture of ground sesame seeds, coriander seeds, cumin and thyme, and season to taste with black pepper and sea salt.
Can I use other greens?
Yes: mustard greens, spinach, even dandelion greens if you enjoy their bitterness. You could add a squeeze of lemon for acidity.

summary: Crepes with roasted French plums, yogurt and honey, made for the #cookforjulia tribute to Julia Child: blender crepe batter rested 2 hours, 1/4 cup per crepe, served with sage-roasted plums (10 minutes at 450°F) and plum-brandy yogurt; serves 6.
glance: blend 1 minute, refrigerate 2 hours; 1/4 cup per crepe
about 1 minute on the first side, about 30 seconds on the second
9 Italian or French plums roasted 10 minutes at 450°F with butter and sage
faq: How do you make Julia Child's crepes?

Put 1 cup cold water, 1 cup cold milk, 4 eggs, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 2 cups sifted flour and 4 tablespoons melted butter in a blender, whiz on high for 1 minute, and refrigerate for 2 hours. It yields about 12 crepes.
How do I get a nice thin crepe?

Pour 1/4 cup of batter into a preheated pan with a tiny bit of butter while tilting and swirling. If it won't spread evenly, work on the swirl, thin the batter a bit, or lower the heat. Expect it to take a few crepes to dial it in.
What pan should I use?

A seriously non-stick one: a well-seasoned cast-iron skillet or an omelet pan with sloped sides. The author uses a 12-inch non-stick omelet pan (a gift from Calphalon) and says not to use metal tools in it.
How do I flip a crepe?
Lift the edge with a silicone spatula and use your fingers to turn it quickly (the author has asbestos fingers), or use two spatulas.
What plums should I use?
A variety with a loose (free) pit and rather dense flesh that can cook without the juices running everywhere. The author used French plums from a neighbor's tree; Italian plums would be just as good.
What can I use instead of slivovitz?
Regular brandy, or 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract. Slivovitz is a plum brandy from the Balkans; or omit the alcohol altogether.
